name: Add-on products must benefit the buyer
description: A dealer may not sell an add-on product that gives the buyer no benefit, such as coverage that duplicates what the buyer already has or a product the buyer cannot use. Add-ons must be offered with their price stated separately, and changes made after the price is agreed need a clear record.

name: Keep deal records for two years
description: Dealers must keep the records of each vehicle sale and financing transaction, including add-on offers, disclosures and signed documents, for two years and produce them on request.

name: GAP price within the permitted limit
description: The price charged for a GAP waiver must stay within the limit set in Civil Code 2982.12. DealTrace compares each GAP price with the limit configured for the group and with the group median.

name: GAP coverage matches the amount financed
description: A GAP waiver must cover the shortfall on the financed amount it is sold with. Coverage limits that leave part of the loan uncovered, or that do not match the contract term, need review.

name: GAP must be able to benefit the buyer (loan-to-value)
description: A GAP waiver should only be sold when the buyer could owe more than the vehicle is worth. When the loan-to-value is low, DealTrace flags the sale for review; the floor used is a group setting, not a statutory figure.

name: GAP disclosures and cancellation rights
description: The buyer must receive the GAP waiver terms in writing, including that the waiver is optional and how to cancel it for a refund. A signed copy must stay in the deal jacket.

name: Texas GAP waiver terms
description: Draft rule for Texas GAP waivers: written terms, optional purchase and refund on early payoff. Not active; Harborline has no Texas rooftops yet.

name: Texas add-on product disclosures
description: Draft rule for Texas add-on disclosures: each optional product priced separately and acknowledged by the buyer before signing.

name: New York optional product consent
description: Draft rule for New York: optional products need the buyer’s express consent, recorded separately from the retail installment contract.
source: New York Personal Property Law, Article 9 (draft mapping)
